## Green Alert Security members other than the Head of Security and the Warden should only carry sidearms, melee weapons, and disabler SMGs on Green Alert. A firearm is considered a sidearm if it can be stored inside of a boot or pocket; otherwise, it is considered a longarm. Active carry is not permitted on Green Alert.
On Green alert, Security HUDs of all forms (including Security Glasses, Medsec HUDs, and Diasec HUDs) are advised, but not required, to be worn. Flash Protection (such as Security Glasses or Corpsman Glasses) are recommended and preferred, but not required.
On Green Alert, armor heavier than an armored vest or coat should not be worn, except for specific threats (such as xeno infestations, temporarily spaced areas, or any work involving the exterior of the station).
Lethal longarms can be issued for specific threats by the Head of Security or the Warden under Green Alert, but must be returned to the armory immediately after. If these threats are not localized (such as xeno infestations or meat anomalies that are most efficiently dealt with by laser rifles and the like) but are instead potentially station-wide or station-threatening, Blue Alert should consider being called. Heavy weapons should never be used under Green Alert.
The Head of Security and the Warden must abide by the same regulations as all other officers, with the exception that they are permitted to carry their unique longarm regardless of alert level. This does not allow the Head of Security or the Warden to wear their unique hardsuits regardless of alert level.
## Blue Alert Security members other than the Head of Security and the Warden should not carry lethal longarms on Blue Alert. Disablers, service weapons, stun batons, and other crowd control weapons are appropriate. Active Carry should be avoided when possible.
One Blue alert, either Security HUDs of any form (including but not limited to Security Glasses, Medsec HUDs, and Diasec HUDs) or flash-protecting items (such as Security Glasses, Security Technician Glasses, or Sun Glasses) are required to be worn. Items which provide both flash protection and HUD elements are recommended.
On Blue alert, armor of any level is recommended, but not required.
Longarms can be issued for specific threats by the Head of Security or the Warden under blue alert, but must be returned to the armory immediately after. Heavy weapons are not authorized for usage on Blue Alert.
## Red Alert
While no warrants are required for any searches including departmental searches on Red Alert, security should prioritize dealing with the active threat(s) over searching crew or departments. Red Alert must not be prolonged after the threat(s) are dealt with in order to search individuals or departments.
On Red alert, either Security HUDs of any form (including but not limited to Security Glasses, Medsec HUDs, and Diasec HUDs) or flash-protecting items (such as Security Glasses, Security Technician Glasses, or Sun Glasses) are required to be worn. Items which provide both flash protection and HUD elements are required, if available.
On Red Alert, all officers are required to wear armor, and are recommended to be fully equipped with as much armor as possible.
Security members can be issued longarms by the Warden or Head of Security, and carry these longarms with them until the alert level is dropped down to Blue or Green again. Heavy weapons may only be carried and used at the discretion of the Head of Security or Warden. These weapons ideally should not be carried in hand unless there is an immediate threat; Red Alert is, however, by definition, an extenuating circumstance, and every officer’s judgement of what an “immediate threat” is is their own.
## Yellow and Orange Alerts
On Yellow/Orange Alerts, security personnel (including the Warden and Head of Security) should defer to members of the Engineering department in all matters that concern Engineering’s ability to restore the station to structural safety. Security should prioritize, to the best of their ability, threats that would impede Engineering personnel from their work, and should assist in diverting non-Engineering personnel away from potential hazards, such as spaced rooms.
If possible, Security personnel should equip hardsuits and utilize Internals to protect them from any environmental hazards. The Warden and Head of Security should distribute this equipment as necessary.
## White Alert
On White Alert, security personnel (including the Warden and Head of Security) should defer to members of the Epistemics department in all matters that concern Epistemics’s ability to address high glimmer or dangerous psionic activity. Security should prioritize, to the best of their ability, threats that would impede Epistemics from their work.
During White Alert, the Mantis or Mystagogue has authority to issue search and arrest warrants as if they were the Head of Security (for the purposes of signing off on such warrants), specifically for individuals suspected of rogue or uncontrolled psionic activity. Personnel that are confirmed to be increasing Glimmer should be charged with Grand Endangerment.
## Violet Alert
On Violet Alert, security personnel (including the Warden and Head of Security) should defer to members of the Medical department in all matters that concern Medical’s ability to contain the infectious hazard. Security should prioritize, to the best of their ability, threats that would impede Medical from their work.
## Delta Alert
Delta Alert, wherein the destruction of the station is imminent, follows all protocol from Red Alert. Security should prioritize assisting in the evacuation of the station. If possible, such as in the case of an unauthorized armed nuclear device aboard the station, security should do whatever is in their power to preserve the station.
## Gamma Alert
Under Gamma Alert, ERT is on board or about to be on board imminently. Security should follow all of their commands and treat the command structure of security as Central Command -> ERT Leader -> ERT -> Captain/Acting Commanding Officer -> Head of Security -> Warden -> Security Mentors and Security Officers (including Corpsman, Detective, and Security Technician) -> Security Cadets.
Generally, arrest, search, and armor/weapons protocol should follow from Red Alert procedure, unless ERT dictates otherwise.
## Octarine Alert
The primary duty of Security during Octarine Alert is to prevent the fabric of local spacetime from rupturing, warping, twisting, imploding, or otherwise changing from its “usual” configuration within the laws of relativity.
On Octarine Alert, wherein the fabric of local spacetime itself is threatened, protocol follows from Red Alert with the exception that orders from members of the Epistemics department (particularly Mystagogue, Chaplain and Mantis) are to be followed to the best of Security’s ability. In addition to this, any members of any department (Security, Command, Epistemics, or otherwise) who have fallen under the influence of noöspheric extremist groups or are overtly sympathetic to such extremists may be disregarded as no longer having any authority over the command structure of Security.
